SMT BINDU O V, PP  THIS CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 25.09.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:

sentences.text:
The challenge in this revision petition is the conviction and sentence rendered against the revision petitioners under Sections 406 and 498A r/w 34 of IPC.
2.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: The revision petitioners are accused Nos.1 and 2 respectively in CC No. 221/2002 on the files of Judicial First Class Magistrate Court I, Parappanangadi.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court I, Parappanangadi
entities.label: COURT

sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text:
They, along with another accused stood trial before that court for committing the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 406 r/w 34 of IPC.
3.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: The prosecution case in brief is as follows; The 1st accused married PW1 on 14.03.2002.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: Thereafter, while living together in the house of the accused, the accused three in number, in furtherance of their common intention, misappropriated Rs.50,000/- and 40 sovereigns of gold ornaments out of the 50 sovereigns of gold ornaments given to PW1 at the time of the marriage.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is also alleged that, the accused subjected PW1 to cruelty demanding more gold and money as dowry.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json
Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: The trial court on an elaborate appreciation of the evidence on record found the 3 rd accused not guilty of the offences alleged and acquitted her.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: But it found the 1 st accused guilty of committing an offence punishable under Section 406 IPC and accused Nos. 1 and 2 guilty of committing the offence punishable under Section 498A r/w 34 IPC.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: Accordingly, it sentenced the 1st accused to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of one year under Section 406 IPC.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text:
It also sentenced the 1st accused to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of 1  years and to pay a fine of Rs.10,000/-
under Section 498A, IPC with a default clause and the 2nd accused to undergo simple imprisonment Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025

sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: 5. Accused Nos. 1 and 2 carried the matter in appeal by filing Crl.Appeal No.369/2010 before the Sessions Court, Manjeri.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: The said court by judgment dated 30.07.2015 dismissed the appeal.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text:
6. Heard the learned counsel for the revision petitioners and the learned public prosecutor.
7.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the revision petitioners submitted that both the trial court and the appellate court have not appreciated the evidence in a proper perspective 2025:KER:72168 and has arrived at a wrong conclusion of guilt against the accused.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: He contended that the evidence of PW1 and PW2 regarding the events are mired with contradictions and there is no credible evidence to prove the factum of misappropriation, as alleged by the prosecution.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: He also argued that the evidence of PW1 would go to show that she is not having a consistent version regarding the events and that the medical evidence adduced does not support the prosecution case.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: 8. Per contra, the learned public prosecutor supported the impugned judgments and contended that there are no grounds to interfere with the same.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: 9. On going through the materials on record, it is seen that the 1st accused, the husband of PW1 has been convicted under Section 406 IPC on the ground that he has misappropriated Rs.50,000/- and 40 sovereigns of gold ornaments from out of the 50 sovereigns given to PW1 at the time of marriage.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: PW1 the victim and PW2 her brother stated that the 1st accused has thus taken away the gold ornaments belonging to PW1 on different occasions by making PW1 believe that the money thus obtained by selling the ornaments will be used for the construction of a 2025:KER:72168 residential house.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is to be taken note that as regards this allegation, the only evidence available is that of PW1 and evidence of PW2 on this aspect is nothing, but hearsay.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: Further, the evidence of PW1 does not show as to when and how much quantity of gold ornaments, the 1 st accused has thus taken away from her and where it was sold.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: In other words, the evidence of PW1 regarding the events of alleged misappropriation of gold is very vague, sans details.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: The prosecution has also not adduced any evidence to show where these gold ornaments have been sold, its quantity and the amount allegedly received by the 1 st accused on such sale.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: At this juncture, I will also take note of another relevant fact, ie; the prosecution has not adduced any convincing evidence to show that at the time of marriage, PW1 was given Rs.50,000/- and 50 sovereigns of gold ornaments as alleged.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: Apart from the interested testimonies of PW1 and PW2, there is no convincing evidence on this aspect.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: Even though the case of the prosecution is that the gold ornaments were purchased from a particular jewellery, not a scrap of paper has been produced to prove the same.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: Further, the prosecution also did not choose to produce at least, the marriage photographs or examine anyone who had 2025:KER:72168 attended the marriage to substantiate its contentions.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: In the light of the evidence as discussed above, I am of the view that the conviction of the 1 st accused under Section 406 IPC cannot be sustained.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text:
10. Coming to the offence under Section 498A IPC, it is the prosecution case that the 1 st and 2nd accused have persistently demanded PW1 and PW2 to bring 25 sovereigns of gold ornaments and Rs.50,000/-, apart from the share in the property of the father of PW1 for the construction of the Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95767305/
3 house.

entities.text: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is their case that, the 1st and 2nd accused have physically and mentally harassed PW1 for this purpose.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: The prosecution is mainly relying upon the evidence of PW1 and PW2 and the evidence of PW5, coupled with Ext.P4 document to prove this fact.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: The evidence of PW1 shows that even though she has jumbled the dates on which the events took place, has specifically deposed regarding the fact that she had called her brother(PW2), when a demand was thus made from the side of accused Nos. 1 and 2.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: Then PW2 came to the house of PW1 and assured the 1 st and 2nd accused that he will try to procure the money within a month.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: Thereafter, on 23.10.2001, PW2 came to the house of PW1 and informed the accused regarding his inability to procure 2025:KER:72168 the money as promised.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is at this point of time, PW1 was physically and mentally harassed by A1 and A2 demanding money and gold.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: On these aspect, it is to be seen that, the evidence of PW1 and PW2 tallies with each.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: Their evidence clearly shows that when PW2 informed A1 and A2 about his inability to procure the money, the 2nd accused dragged PW1 to the courtyard of the house and threatened her stating that the 1st accused will be married to a more beautiful woman than her's, if the demand is not met.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: The first accused also caught hold of her hair and assaulted her.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text:
At that time,
when PW1 demanded back the gold ornaments and money she had given to them, the 1 st accused slapped her on her face and the 2 nd accused punched her on her stomach.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: PW2 timely intervened and took PW1 to the hospital, where she was treated for two days.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is to be seen that even though these witnesses have been cross examined in extenso, no material contradictions have been brought out to disbelieve their testimonies on these aspects.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: Further, the evidence of PW5, the doctor coupled with Ext.P4 wound certificate, goes to show that PW1 had approached her seeking medical aid, immediately after the incident at about 5.00 p.m, with an allegation of assault by 2025:KER:72168 her husband and in-laws and with complaints of pain on her head and lower abdomen.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: The afore evidence also gives credence and support to the version of PW1 and PW2 regarding the events which transpired on 23.10.2001.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text:
In the light of the afore discussions, I find that both the trial court and the appellate court have not committed any illegality or error in appreciating the evidence on record on this aspect and in reaching a conclusion of guilt against the 1 st and 2nd accused, under Section 498A of IPC.
11.
sentences._hearing_file: Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 25 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: Now the question to be considered is regarding the sentence.
